items.evidence: The AC#1 test passes. It asserts that seat 4 is Maniac before the edit, that the result is Custom, that config.lineUp is Custom, and that the styles are [null, TAG, CS, Rock, Rock, TAG]. Holdout: Mixed 6 user 1 seat 4 changed to Rock gives Custom. Exhaustive single-seat edits (every preset, size, user seat, bot seat and style) give Custom iff the style differs. 0 failures.

The AC#2 test passes and counts 162. Holdout: my own clockwise seat walk and preset rules reproduce seatLineUp exactly for all 162 line-ups. resolveLineUpName returns the preset for each of them. For each line-up I also resolved against all 3 presets and compared with my own expected value (pattern equality against that chosen preset only). All match, including heads-up Mixed/Tough.

The AC#3 test passes: Soft 6/1 seat 3 Rock→TAG gives Custom, then back to Rock gives Soft. Holdout: edit-then-revert on every bot seat with every style across all 162 line-ups always restores the preset name.

The AC#4 test passes with a full toEqual against the spec literal, and the unedited case gives Mixed. Holdout: 3240 random multi-seat edits checked lineUp against my own expected name, players, userSeat, every seat's number/kind/name/style (user = 'You', null style), the cash stake and speed, a random valid button, and unmutated input. The output seat objects are fresh (no aliasing). Cash output keys are exactly button,gameType,lineUp,players,seats,speed,stake,userSeat.

The unit test passes. It covers default seat 5 Maniac at seat 2 changed to Rock (Custom), Mixed edited to the Soft pattern (Custom under Mixed, Soft under Soft), Tough 2/2 under Mixed (Mixed), renamed bots ignored, the sit-and-go base with no stake key, and base/seats unmutated (structuredClone compare). Holdout: a sit-and-go base with button 4 and Tough 4/4 gives keys without stake, gameType sit-and-go, lineUp Tough. The base is unmutated and DEFAULT_SESSION_CONFIG is unchanged.

The unit test passes and covers every section 5 message, plus two-rule cases that pin the check order. Holdout: 24 malformed-seat cases checked through both functions for instanceof RangeError and the exact message. They covered [], duplicates, seat 0, gaps, reversed order, a lone user (size error), zero or three users, null style/name, 11 seats, Custom/Bogus presets, and order combinations (numbering before user count before bot fields before size/preset). Inputs were unmutated. Button 0, 7, 2.5, -1, NaN, Infinity, '3', null and undefined all throw 'Button must be a seat at the table', while 1 and 6 are accepted. Heads-up with the default button 6 throws (A-4). Seat errors take precedence over a bad button.
